## Executive verdict

Murmur has unusually strong workflow ideas: domain-specific skills, independent verification, a dedicated lock reviewer, incident-derived guardrails, a versioned learnings loop, and one local CI entry point. The knowledge base is better than most agent setups.

The control plane is not yet trustworthy enough to call a top workflow. The central problem is not a lack of agents. It is the gap between what the workflow says is enforced and what is actually enforced.

The audit found eight stop-ship classes:

1. The canonical release instructions contradict the binding release policy and can produce a blocked, unnotarized, or incorrectly signed release.
2. The dev restart skill can kill the currently running installed Murmur application.
3. GitHub does not require CI for merge, administrators can bypass the classic branch protection, and GitHub secret scanning/push protection are disabled on this public repository.
4. The green CI gate does not compile or test the new murmur-brain workspace member, does not run the existing Playwright suite, and can hide a broken AI provider behind a stub.
5. The machine-readable Definition of Done is advisory, usually inactive, and not bound to the reviewed diff.
6. Worktree and process isolation are not real: fixed ports, absolute checkout paths, blanket process kills, and git add -A make concurrent work unsafe.
7. Privacy and runtime claims in autoloaded instructions contradict the code, including a now-obsolete database-recovery instruction that could prompt unnecessary manipulation of production data.
8. The shared murmur-protocol source is taken from a mutable sibling checkout locally and an unpinned sibling default branch in CI, so one Murmur commit is not reproducible against one protocol revision.

The right next move is a safety and truth repair, not a larger fleet. After the P0 controls are real, the existing skills can support an excellent workflow with only a few thin role adapters and two or three focused additions.

## Stop-ship findings

### P0.1 — the canonical release path is internally contradictory and unsafe

Codex currently ignores .codex/agents/release-engineer.toml because line 30 contains an invalid TOML escape. Merely repairing that syntax would activate an obsolete procedure.

The deeper problem is shared by both tool surfaces:

- .agents/skills/release-murmur/SKILL.md:161-178 tells the agent to run the forbidden macOS keychain CLI and sign with codesign --deep.
- The same skill at lines 222-241 explicitly permits publishing a signed but unnotarized DMG.
- It references the removed src-tauri/Cargo.lock at lines 93 and 99; the workspace lock is now Cargo.lock at repository root.
- It hardcodes old release history and an absolute checkout.
- .claude/skills/release-murmur carries the same procedure.
- The active Claude release role also uses the forbidden keychain CLI, deep signing, old target paths, git add -A, and a signed-only fallback.

The root charters are internally contradictory too: AGENTS.md:100 and CLAUDE.md:98 tell the agent to derive the identity with security find-identity; the immediately following rule forbids agent-shell security commands. The intended policy across AGENTS.md:97-103 is:

- notarization is mandatory;
- sign nested helpers inside-out;
- never use deep signing;
- never run keychain CLI operations from the agent shell;
- use the existing notary profile;
- never publish signed-only.

The nominal canonical script is not yet a clean escape hatch. scripts/macos-sign-notarize.sh:

- invokes the forbidden security cms command;
- accepts a certificate name even though the binding rule requires the identity hash;
- accepts Apple credentials directly in command arguments rather than requiring the existing keychain profile;
- runs a deep verification form that the guard itself rejects;
- can be invoked through a wrapper command that prevents the string hook from observing its internal forbidden command.

**Required target:** one release operator script with no keychain CLI call, a user-supplied identity hash, inside-out explicit helper signing, the murmur notary profile only, mandatory notarization/stapling/spctl success, root Cargo.lock, and no signed-only publish branch. The release agent should be a thin preflight/orchestration adapter, not another copy of the runbook.

### P0.2 — the dev skill can kill the installed production application

At audit time, /Applications/Murmur.app/Contents/MacOS/Murmur was the real owner of 127.0.0.1:8765.

.agents/skills/tauri-dev/SKILL.md:69-76 instructs:

- blanket pkill by the product process name;
- blanket pkill by tauri-dev command text;
- kill -9 of every owner of ports 1420 and 8765.

The MCP server uses a fixed port in src-tauri/src/mcp.rs:15-16 and has no debug override. Following the skill would terminate the user's installed app and can destroy an active meeting/session. The same pattern also appears in the release skill.

**Required target:** task-owned PID files, executable/worktree identity checks, graceful TERM with bounded wait, KILL only for a PID created by that task, and a debug-only MCP port override or default-off MCP in dev. Never free a port by killing an unknown owner. Full-app dev runs should be an exclusive lane; mocked FE tests should use private ports.

### P0.3 — GitHub is not the enforcement boundary the workflow assumes

Live repository settings for the public murmur-io/murmur repository showed:

- required_status_checks is null;
- classic branch protection has enforce_admins false;
- the pull-request rule requires zero approvals;
- the active ruleset only blocks deletion and non-fast-forward updates;
- no ruleset requires the CI check;
- GitHub secret scanning is disabled;
- secret-scanning push protection is disabled;
- non-provider secret patterns and validity checks are disabled;
- Dependabot security updates are disabled.

The exact current CI check name is gate (full ci.sh — release parity). A local hook is therefore carrying responsibility it cannot safely carry, while an administrator can merge without the gate.

**Required target:** a branch ruleset requiring pull requests and the exact CI status, applying to administrators except for an explicit break-glass policy, plus conversation resolution. Enable GitHub secret scanning, push protection, validity checks, and non-provider patterns. Keep local hooks as fast feedback, never as the security boundary.

### P0.4 — green CI does not verify the product now being shipped

#### The new brain sidecar is outside the gate

Root Cargo.toml defines src-tauri and crates/murmur-brain as workspace members but sets default-members to src-tauri. scripts/ci.sh runs cargo only from src-tauri. The brain is built explicitly only by Tauri beforeDevCommand/beforeBuildCommand.

Consequently, the regular CI gate does not run the five murmur-brain tests and does not independently lint/build that package. A broken on-device brain can merge behind a green gate.

#### The UI E2E suite is outside the gate

Playwright discovered 122 tests in 58 files on the initial pass and 126 in 59 files during final verification, including lock/leak/error-state coverage. The count changed because the working tree was concurrently active. Neither scripts/ci.sh nor the GitHub workflow invokes npm run test:e2e.

playwright.config.ts also uses:

- fixed port 4210;
- reuseExistingServer true;
- Chromium only, although the packaged app uses WKWebView;
- trace on first retry while retries are zero, so a trace can never be captured.

The verifier journal records a real wrong-worktree server incident.

#### The headless provider step is not honest

src-tauri/examples/e2e_core.rs:77-95 directly constructs ClaudeCodeProvider. If Claude is available, it sends the synthetic transcript through the ambient CLI outside the app's central consent/redaction/ledger factory. On any provider error it silently substitutes a stub and still passes.

On GitHub, logs show the stub path, so a completely broken provider remains green. On this Mac, claude is installed, so a local full CI run can make two unexpected cloud calls. The text is synthetic, but the workflow violates its own no-surprise-egress contract.

scripts/e2e-core.sh also downloads a mutable main-branch Whisper model without checksum into the same Application Support model directory used by the product.

**Required target:** explicitly lint/test/build murmur-brain; make Playwright hermetic and add a bounded critical Chromium plus WebKit gate; use a deterministic local fake provider by default; move real-provider smoke to an explicit opt-in job through the production egress seam; pin the model revision and checksum in an isolated test cache.

### P0.5 — the Definition of Done can attest to a different or stale diff

.codex/hooks/finish-guard.sh defaults to advisory. It exits immediately when no current task pointer or matching branch directory exists. No workflow initializes .codex/tmp/.current-task, and it is absent now.

Synthetic behavior:

- missing verdict in advisory mode allows;
- enforce mode blocks only when a task happens to resolve;
- a PASS with deliberately wrong hashes and ancient timestamp allows;
- a lock-sensitive change allows when the manual .lock-touched marker is omitted;
- bare JSON containing only verdict PASS allows.

The final inventory found 155 ignored verdict artifacts. Only one had any head SHA; zero had a staged-diff hash. Existing Codex PASS files contain only verdict, findings, and prose summary.

The guard also has no selftests. The current hook selftest covers block-bash and secret-scan only.

**Required target:** stage only explicitly owned files, compute a canonical SHA-256 of the staged binary diff, and require schema version, task ID, repo/worktree identity, base SHA, diff hash, reviewer role, timestamp, commands/evidence, and risk flags. The guard must recompute the hash immediately before commit. Lock/egress/protocol requirements must be derived from the staged paths and content, not a manual marker.

### P0.6 — concurrency guidance can commit or verify another agent's work

The current tree is heavily dirty from concurrent work, yet ship-feature still says git add -A. That can stage unrelated work and commit another agent's changes.

Several canonical skills start by changing to /Users/jakubgawronski/Projects/meetnotes. A worker dispatched in an isolated worktree can silently leave it and operate on the primary dirty checkout.

Playwright and full dev use fixed ports. Skills recommend parallel builders but have no ownership manifest, no process registry, and no machine-wide Cargo semaphore. The one-Cargo policy exists only in Claude's pr-program.

For sibling murmur-server work, hooks remain rooted in the meetnotes session and inspect meetnotes state; they cannot be assumed to protect a server commit.

**Required target:** one write owner per worktree, explicit owned paths, no git add -A, repo/worktree fingerprinting, private test ports, one machine-wide Cargo wrapper, and a distinct session/control plane for each repository. Cross-repo protocol work needs a two-repo manifest, not workdir switching under one repo's hooks.

### P0.7 — autoloaded privacy and recovery rules contradict current code

AGENTS.md:78, CLAUDE.md:76, and both active researcher surfaces say claude_code sends nothing off-device. The code is explicit:

- claude_code, Anthropic, and Gateway are cloud;
- remote Ollama is cloud;
- loopback Ollama and on-device connections are local;
- unknown provider IDs fail safe as cloud;
- cloud providers must pass consent, redaction, and the egress ledger.

The root charters also state that dev and release collide on one shared database and prescribe restoring a plaintext backup. Current src-tauri/src/state.rs:15-38 proves this was fixed: debug/dev uses MeetNotes-dev while release uses MeetNotes. Keeping the obsolete recovery rule can cause unnecessary manipulation of production data.

Other autoloaded volatile claims are also false:

- shipped version 0.6.4 versus current public release and manifests at 1.0.1;
- Angular 18 versus Angular 22;
- experimental zoneless provider versus stable provideZonelessChangeDetection;
- allowSignalWrites requirements removed since Angular 19;
- default Whisper small versus conditional turbo/small selection;
- build env under src-tauri/.cargo versus the workspace-root .cargo;
- one commands.rs file versus the commands module directory;
- in-process reason/mistral.rs versus the murmur-brain sidecar.

**Required target:** correct privacy and destructive-recovery claims immediately. Remove volatile versions, counts, model defaults, and file-line maps from root charters. Point to code symbols/manifests or enforce generated facts instead.

### P0.8 — the shared protocol dependency is not reproducible

src-tauri/Cargo.toml:114 compiles murmur-protocol from ../../murmur-server/crates/murmur-protocol. The source therefore lives outside the Murmur commit and Cargo.lock cannot bind it to a server revision.

The two execution environments are both mutable:

- locally, the sibling checkout was on feat/entitlement-backbone at b6a6cf73d2fdac2e1c470a1d860f255849d07b7a with uncommitted changes in multiple murmur-protocol files during final verification;
- CI uses a depth-one clone of the sibling repository without an explicit ref, so it compiles whatever the default branch points to at run time.

The same Murmur SHA can therefore pass or fail against different protocol source, and a local PASS can include uncommitted sibling code absent from both PRs. This is a build-reproducibility and wire-compatibility failure at the E2EE sharing seam.

The checkout also populates known_hosts with live ssh-keyscan output. That does not authenticate the first connection against a pre-trusted GitHub host key and is a separate P1 supply-chain weakness.

**Required target:** commit a reviewed protocol-revision contract, make CI fetch and checkout that exact sibling SHA, and make local preflight reject a mismatched or protocol-dirty sibling unless the task manifest explicitly owns both repositories. Include both repository SHAs and the protocol tree state in review receipts and release provenance. Replace live ssh-keyscan trust-on-first-use with GitHub's published host keys/fingerprints.

## Codex versus Claude

Neither tree is the winner. Claude is more current in several knowledge surfaces; Codex has the stronger current platform primitives but is not using them.

| Surface | Codex today | Claude today | Target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root instructions | AGENTS.md plus on-demand project rules | CLAUDE.md plus Claude rules | Short AGENTS.md canon; CLAUDE.md imports it and adds only Claude deltas |
| Rules | Four files; Angular and workflow materially stale | Four files; Angular newer | One authored rule set with generated/linted adapters |
| Skills | 16 neutral skills visible; learn/curate native | 15 skills plus two commands; pr-program only here | One neutral skill source and parity manifest |
| Agents | 7 files, 6 load | 11 load | Thin role adapters; knowledge remains in skills/rules |
| Permissions | No active project credential deny; parent inheritance | Active deny list plus broad local allows | User profiles for audit/edit/runtime; role-specific least privilege |
| Hooks | Active and trusted | Active | Canonical scripts, separate wiring, expanded tests |
| DoD | Advisory/fail-open | Advisory/fail-open | Hash-bound staged receipt plus required remote CI |
| Learnings | Older copies | Newer copies | One canonical versioned store, deterministic small injection |
| Worktrees | Supported by platform but undermined by paths/ports | Better native worktree concepts, same repo hazards | Worktree manifest, bootstrap, ownership, private resources |
| CI knowledge | Agent/skill prose stale | Agent/skill prose stale | scripts/ci.sh plus a machine-audited manifest |
| Release | Broken role and unsafe shared skill | Loading role and unsafe shared skill | One safe operator; thin adapters only |

### Context cost and discovery

The initial name-plus-description metadata is already over the documented 8,000-character fallback budget:

- .agents/skills valid entries: 8,443 characters, excluding the malformed skill;
- .claude/skills: 8,774 characters;
- system skills add more.

Official Codex guidance says descriptions are shortened first and skills can eventually be omitted from the initial list. This makes the missing root router more dangerous. Descriptions should be one or two trigger-first sentences with explicit boundaries; all detail belongs in the body.

The duplicated prompt corpus is also large:

- Codex agent prompts: about 70 KB;
- Claude agent prompts: about 134 KB;
- root plus rule corpora: roughly 56-60 KB per surface;
- most duplicated skills differ only by product paths, while a few critical copies have semantic drift.

Do not create a third long prompt layer.

## Current global Codex posture

The user-level Codex installation is healthy except for the project role warning:

- codex-cli 0.144.6; 0.145.0 available;
- global default model is a high-end private/local selection with max effort;
- normal CLI baseline reports restricted filesystem/network and OnRequest approvals;
- this audit session was explicitly overridden to unrestricted filesystem and no approvals;
- three remote MCP servers are globally configured;
- no user [agents] limits are set, so behavior depends on defaults/platform caps;
- auth storage mode is File; auth.json is permission 0600;
- approximately 743 MB under ~/.codex, including about 514 MB active sessions;
- doctor reported 64 active rollout files and zero archived at audit time;
- five system skills, no custom personal skill set, and only a cached curated plugin;
- global hooks are local Superset notification hooks and do not carry Murmur's security policy.

Recommended user-level changes, after repo controls are repaired:

    cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring"

    [agents]
    max_threads = 4
    max_depth = 1
    job_max_runtime_seconds = 1800

Also:

- create explicit audit, edit, runtime-audit, and release permission profiles;
- deny credential paths and production Murmur data by default;
- make production-data access an explicit user-selected audit profile;
- disable or role-scope Linear/Figma/Notion MCP when not needed;
- archive completed sessions and use ephemeral mode for one-shot scheduled checks;
- remove stale trusted temporary test entries;
- do not commit personal home paths or MCP endpoints to the repository.

Custom agent files should set reasoning effort and sandbox intent. Do not commit a private/short-lived model slug. A practical policy:

| Role | Sandbox intent | Effort | Knowledge preload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Researcher/explorer | Read-only | Medium/high | research |
| AI architect | Read-only | High | design-ai-seam |
| App performance | Read-only by default | High | app-perf-audit |
| Model performance | Read-only by default | High | ondevice-model-perf |
| Retrieval architect | Read-only | High | retrieval-memory-brain |
| Rust/Angular builder | Workspace-write in isolated worktree | High | matching rules/skill |
| Adversarial/spec/security reviewer | Read-only on an immutable staged snapshot | High | matching checklist |
| Bug reproducer | Workspace-write in isolated repro worktree; cannot fix | High | reproduction contract |
| Release preflight | Read-only | High | release-murmur |

Parent live permission overrides can supersede role defaults. Therefore the orchestrator must choose a safe parent lane before delegation; TOML prose alone cannot guarantee isolation.

## Skill routing that matches the repository

The root router currently lists only part of the installed skill set and does not define precedence for overlapping triggers.

Use this decision ladder:

1. Product/market/feasibility question: research.
2. Accepted AI capability and seam placement: design-ai-seam.
3. Retrieval/chunking/embeddings/reranking/memory quality: retrieval-memory-brain.
4. UI/IPC/startup/jank/heat/OOM outside model runtime: app-perf-audit.
5. GGUF/Whisper/Metal/quant/KV/model RAM or thermals: ondevice-model-perf.
6. Implementation or bug fix: ship-feature.
7. CI diagnosis: ci-maintenance.
8. Add/change a CI gate: add-ci-gate.
9. GitHub workflow/caching/action maintenance: github-actions.
10. Dev app lifecycle: tauri-dev, after process ownership is fixed.
11. Release: sync-release-copy, then release-murmur.
12. Backend deploy/ops only: deploy-murmur-server.
13. Divergent ideation: dreaming.

Three repo-visible skill/workflow additions make sense after P0:

### protocol-sync

Trigger on accounts, OPAQUE, sharing envelopes, invitations, Org sync, wire format, or murmur-protocol changes. It should:

- open both meetnotes and the sibling murmur-server as separate controlled roots;
- identify the shared-crate compatibility change;
- define client/server version and rollout order;
- run both repositories' targeted tests;
- require privacy/protocol review;
- coordinate two PRs without switching a single task's hook root;
- provide rollback and backward-compatibility evidence.

There is a deploy skill, but no safe feature-change protocol for this load-bearing cross-repo seam.

### egress-security-review

The existing design skill requires lock-security-reviewer for egress changes, but the current lock reviewer checklist does not audit provider/connector consent, redaction, ledger, remote Ollama, Gateway, or raw network-client bypass.

Add a focused egress checklist skill and load it into a renamed privacy-security reviewer, or add a thin egress reviewer role. Avoid a generic security agent. Risk classification should require this review for providers, connectors, MCP tools, sharing, direct reqwest/network clients, and any new outgoing payload field.

### Port pr-program

Port the proven Claude-only intent:

- exactly one local Cargo owner machine-wide;
- read-only fan-out only;
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 for local targeted builds;
- sequential PRs;
- remote full CI;
- explicit-path staging;
- no worktree remove --force;
- liveness and dirty/unmerged checks before cleanup.

## Agent changes

### Restore as thin Codex adapters

These Claude roles map directly to existing neutral skills and should not duplicate their long prompts:

- ai-systems-architect -> design-ai-seam;
- app-perf-engineer -> app-perf-audit;
- memory-retrieval-architect -> retrieval-memory-brain;
- model-perf-engineer -> ondevice-model-perf.

Each adapter needs only a narrow trigger, sandbox/effort, selected skill, and output contract.

### Add two behaviorally distinct roles

1. **bug-reproducer** — establishes a minimal RED with exact evidence and never implements the fix. Any mutation occurs in its own worktree.
2. **spec-coverage-reviewer** — compares user intent/spec/acceptance criteria to the staged diff and wiring before the adversarial code review.

### Reshape existing roles

- Replace release-engineer with a thin preflight/operator adapter after the release script is safe.
- Keep ci-cd-engineer narrow: it owns pipeline mutation/review, while knowledge stays in the three CI skills.
- Make adversarial-verifier consume an immutable staged snapshot and return its verdict to the parent.
- Make the parent write evidence artifacts, so read-only reviewers are mechanically read-only.
- Expand/rename lock-security-reviewer into a privacy reviewer with separately selected lock and egress checklists.
- Remove exact test/command counts and stale file-line anchors from all role prompts.

## Hook and evidence architecture

Official Codex documentation explicitly says specialized tool paths can opt out and hooks are useful guardrails, not a complete enforcement boundary. The current design language overstates them.

### Observed hook gaps

The simple selftests pass, but synthetic variants allow:

- git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/murmur;
- git -C . push origin murmur;
- absolute-path keychain executable forms;
- cargo +stable clippy --all-targets;
- several long-form or quoted recursive-delete forms;
- git -C commit paths around commit detection;
- sk-proj and ghs secret shapes.

Harmless commands containing forbidden text in an rg pattern or comment are blocked.

The scripts themselves use relative repository state. Manual/subdirectory invocation can therefore inspect the wrong scope. The current Codex host was observed normalizing project hook cwd to the root, so this is not claimed as a proven live Codex exploit; it remains a portability and Claude/manual-hook defect.

### Target evidence schema

One task manifest per write worktree:

    schema_version
    task_id
    repo_realpath
    git_common_dir
    branch
    base_sha
    dependency_revisions: murmur_protocol_sha
    owned_paths
    risk_flags: lock, egress, protocol, runtime, ui
    required_checks
    created_at

Before review:

1. Stage only owned paths.
2. Hash the complete staged binary diff.
3. Freeze mutation while reviewers run.
4. Record each command, exit status, duration, and relevant artifact.

Each verdict repeats:

    schema_version
    task_id
    reviewer_role
    base_sha
    dependency_revisions
    staged_diff_sha256
    risk_scope
    verdict
    findings
    commands
    created_at

The commit guard recomputes the staged hash. The remote required CI then binds evidence to the resulting commit SHA.

### Enforcement layers

1. Sandbox/permission profile: credential and production-data boundary.
2. Task/worktree ownership: mutation boundary.
3. Agent hooks: fast UX and incident guardrails.
4. Real Git pre-commit hook: local cross-client convenience, still bypassable.
5. GitHub push protection and required branch rules: authoritative remote boundary.
6. CI: deterministic repository truth.

## Honest CI target

Keep scripts/ci.sh as the single definition of what green means, but repair its scope.

Recommended order:

1. agent-config-audit and canonical hook selftests;
2. exact murmur-protocol revision/clean-tree contract plus its tests;
3. Swift sidecar typechecks;
4. app clippy/tests;
5. murmur-brain clippy/tests/build;
6. pinned cargo audit/deny;
7. app build;
8. Angular lint/build;
9. hermetic Playwright critical Chromium suite;
10. critical WebKit suite;
11. deterministic audio/ASR/export E2E with fake provider and checksum-pinned model.

Operational fixes:

- rust-cache workspace mapping . -> target, supported by the action's documented workspace-to-target syntax;
- fetch the sibling repository at the reviewed protocol SHA and use GitHub-published known-host keys rather than live ssh-keyscan output;
- pin cargo-audit and cargo-deny and install once;
- no ambient Claude/API provider in normal CI;
- separate explicit cloud smoke with synthetic payload, production egress wrapper, and clear ledger;
- private port, reuseExistingServer false, bounded workers, traces/screenshots on failure;
- emit step timings and a compact coverage statement;
- add npm high/critical production audit after a RED-before-GREEN policy test;
- keep live microphone, ScreenCaptureKit/TCC, Touch ID, keychain ACL, packaged WKWebView, and notarization outside headless claims.

The latest successful PR run took 20m18s. Logs show the obsolete target cache despite a cache hit and about 4m20s spent recompiling preinstalled audit tools. Fixing those should finance the missing deterministic checks.

## Target architecture

The neutral layer should own knowledge once; each product surface should own only loading syntax.

    .agents/
      skills/                  canonical workflows and domain maps
      rules/                   canonical durable rules
      learnings/               canonical auditable lessons
      workflow-contract.yaml   roles, routing, parity, risk classifiers, evidence schema

    AGENTS.md                  short durable charter and router
    CLAUDE.md                  import AGENTS.md plus Claude-only deltas

    .codex/agents/             thin TOML role adapters
    .claude/agents/            thin Claude role adapters
    .codex/hooks.json          Codex wiring only
    .claude/settings.json      Claude wiring/permissions only

    scripts/agent-config-audit.sh
    scripts/task-init.sh
    scripts/task-receipt.sh
    scripts/with-cargo-lock.sh
    scripts/dev-process-owner.sh

Do not migrate everything with unverified symlinks in one change. Introduce a parity manifest and check first, then move one class at a time. Generated adapters or a deterministic check are safer than two hand-edited copies.

## Target execution workflow

    User intent
      -> classify read-only vs mutation and risk flags
      -> choose the skill ladder
      -> initialize task manifest and isolated worktree
      -> assert exact sibling revision and clean/owned protocol tree when required
      -> research/spec
      -> bug reproducer establishes RED when applicable
      -> one writer per owned path; one Cargo owner machine-wide
      -> stage explicit owned paths
      -> spec-coverage review on staged hash
      -> adversarial review on same hash
      -> lock / egress / protocol review when classified
      -> targeted tests and runtime evidence
      -> full honest CI locally only when safe
      -> commit guard recomputes hash
      -> PR
      -> required remote CI
      -> merge
      -> retain compact PII-free receipt
      -> add one operator-approved learning when warranted

Parallelism policy:

- parallel: read-only research, independent scans, documentation comparison, log analysis;
- serial or isolated: builders, repro mutation, verifier mutation, dev app, release;
- globally one local Cargo process;
- never run a mutating verifier beside a security reviewer on the same dirty tree;
- max_depth 1; max_threads 4 is enough for root plus three read-heavy specialists.

## Prioritized rollout

### Wave 0 — immediate safety

1. Enable required CI and GitHub secret scanning/push protection.
2. Remove the root charter's security find-identity contradiction and quarantine release role/skills until the canonical script has no forbidden path.
3. Remove blanket process kills before the next tauri-dev run.
4. Correct privacy, DB-isolation, Angular, version, target-path, and CI truth.
5. Remove git add -A and absolute primary-checkout changes from write skills.
6. Add murmur-brain to CI.
7. Pin the murmur-protocol revision across local preflight, CI, receipts, and release provenance.
8. Make normal headless E2E deterministic and no-egress.

**Exit:** no command in active release/dev guidance contradicts a binding rule; installed Murmur survives a dev preflight; one Murmur SHA resolves to one reviewed protocol SHA; required remote status cannot be bypassed normally; no ambient cloud call occurs in CI.

### Wave 1 — deterministic contract

1. Add scripts/agent-config-audit.sh and wire it early into scripts/ci.sh using the add-ci-gate discipline.
2. Parse TOML/JSON/YAML/shell and run both hook matrices.
3. Reject stale critical tokens and dead repo paths.
4. Add task manifest, staged-diff hash, automatic risk classifier, and full finish-guard selftests.
5. Fix hook command variants and root anchoring.
6. Add one machine-wide Cargo wrapper/semaphore with owner metadata.
7. Make Playwright private-port/no-reuse and add the critical CI suite.
8. Replace live ssh-keyscan trust with GitHub's published host keys/fingerprints.
9. Fix rust-cache and pinned tool install.

**Exit:** deliberately malformed agent config, stale/wrong verdict, omitted lock/egress review, wrong-worktree Playwright server, and second local Cargo owner all fail deterministically.

### Wave 2 — one source of truth

1. Make AGENTS.md short and durable.
2. Import it from CLAUDE.md.
3. Add workflow-contract parity checks.
4. Migrate rules/learnings one category at a time.
5. Refresh sidecar-era performance maps.
6. Shorten every skill description below the discovery budget.
7. Port pr-program.
8. Add role-specific permissions/effort and four thin specialist adapters.

**Exit:** one knowledge edit updates or invalidates both product surfaces; Codex doctor has zero startup warnings; no dead module path remains in active guidance.

### Wave 3 — higher-quality autonomy

1. Add bug-reproducer and spec-coverage-reviewer.
2. Add protocol-sync and focused egress-security review.
3. Add task-owned process/port registry and safe cleanup.
4. Add compact learning injection at subagent start.
5. Pilot local Codex review against five PRs; measure useful findings and false positives before making it policy.

**Exit:** accepted features are checked for both requested behavior and adversarial correctness on one immutable snapshot.

### Wave 4 — maintenance

1. Weekly report-only workflow-health automation in an isolated worktree.
2. Dry-run scratch/session retention report and safe janitor.
3. Grouped Dependabot for npm, Cargo, and GitHub Actions with a low PR limit.
4. Optional plugin only if the workflow is intentionally distributed across repositories or a team.

## What not to add

- No plugin for this single evolving repository yet.
- No mass MCP installation or ambient connector expansion.
- No Playwright MCP as a substitute for the existing test harness.
- No global Stop hook that launches full CI.
- No nested agent fan-out.
- No parallel local Cargo builders.
- No long copied Claude prompts as Codex roles.
- No second generic security agent without a distinct checklist.
- No autonomous deletion of scratch/worktrees/sessions.
- No worktree remove --force.
- No signed-only release path.
- No hardcoded current versions, test counts, command counts, model defaults, or unstable line numbers in root prompts.
- No assumption that a hook is a complete enforcement boundary.

## Official guidance and web research

The recommendations above align with current primary guidance:

- OpenAI says AGENTS.md should provide durable project guidance, with skills, memories, MCP, and subagents serving different layers: [Codex AGENTS.md](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md) and [customization overview](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/overview).
- Codex custom agents support model, reasoning, sandbox, MCP, and skill overrides; max depth defaults to one, and read-heavy fan-out is the safer use of parallelism: [Codex subagents](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents).
- Skills use progressive disclosure and an initial context budget; descriptions should be concise and trigger-first: [Build Codex skills](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills).
- Codex supports PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SubagentStart, and SubagentStop, but explicitly says hooks are useful guardrails rather than a complete enforcement boundary: [Codex hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks).
- Codex permission profiles can deny exact/glob credential and production-data reads: [Codex permissions](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions) and [sandboxing](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing).
- Project MCP servers can be scoped instead of globally ambient: [Codex MCP](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp).
- A local skill is the right authoring unit while one repository is evolving; plugins are for stable distribution: [Codex plugins](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-plugins).
- Scheduled work can use isolated worktrees, and finished sessions can be archived: [Codex automations](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/automations) and [worktrees](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/git-worktrees).
- Local memory is a recall layer, not the sole home of binding team rules: [Codex memories](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/memories).
- Claude supports importing AGENTS.md into CLAUDE.md, path-scoped rules, tool allowlists, skill preloading, subagent memory, hooks, and worktree isolation: [Claude memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory), [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents), [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions), and [worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees).
- The Agent Skills standard supports one portable skill package with name/description plus progressively loaded resources: [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).
- Swatinem rust-cache documents workspace-to-target mappings and defaults each workspace to its own target directory, confirming the current src-tauri mapping is stale after the root-workspace move: [rust-cache README](https://github.com/Swatinem/rust-cache).
- GitHub rulesets and secret push protection are the appropriate remote controls: [GitHub rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets) and [push protection](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/protecting-pushes-with-secret-scanning).
- GitHub publishes exact known-host entries and fingerprints, so CI does not need to trust unauthenticated live ssh-keyscan output: [GitHub SSH key fingerprints](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/githubs-ssh-key-fingerprints).

Live public evidence:

- current shipped release: [Murmur v1.0.1](https://github.com/murmur-io/murmur/releases/tag/v1.0.1);
- recent 20m18s CI run used for timing analysis: [GitHub Actions run 29826024324](https://github.com/murmur-io/murmur/actions/runs/29826024324).

## Limitations and safe handoff

This audit ran against a dirty concurrent worktree whose Rust and Playwright counts changed during the audit. The sibling murmur-server checkout and its protocol dirtiness were inspected read-only. Application/configuration files were not changed, production data was not read, the installed application was not stopped, GitHub settings were not mutated, and full local CI was deliberately not launched.

Before implementation, re-check every dirty release/dev/recording file and preserve concurrent ownership. The safest implementation sequence is remote merge protection, release/dev quarantine, truth repair, and deterministic config checks before any new autonomous role is added.
